audit.why: 51.76% over 823 games — narrowly Ambessa's, decided almost entirely by whether Public Execution lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with the prose at every single stage. It says Skill at level 1 where whys[0] says 'concede the opening'; Jayce at 2 and 3 where whys[1] says 'keep it even' and whys[2] says 'you trade evenly'; Skill at 4-5 where whys[3] calls it 'your weakest window'; Skill at 6 and Jayce at first item where whys[4] and whys[5] both describe Ambessa kills; and Jayce at two items where late says 'It evens back out'. Seven stages, seven mismatches.
audit.why: The lane's real shape is a poke phase he owns, a level 3-2 stretch that is genuinely contested, and two Ambessa stages once the 1250-unit blink exists, settling into a skill lane late.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Jayce / Skill / Skill / Jayce / Ambessa / Ambessa / Skill in both layers — Ambessa 2, Jayce 2, Skill 3, which fits 51.76% and matches every why on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ambessa's level 6 is credited to 'the R-passive armor pen plus heal' and late to 'your R-heal sustain', none of which exists in Riot's text for Public Execution or Drakehound's Step. Jayce's own most important spike — the weapon swap itself — is never described mechanically.
audit.why: Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer is a 6-second cooldown with two very different first-attack effects: swapping to cannon makes the first attack reduce the target's Armor and Magic Resist, and swapping to hammer gives Jayce increased Armor and Magic Resist. Against a champion who deals only physical damage, that second half is the whole late-game story, and it is available roughly every six seconds.
audit.corrected: Penetration and healing claims removed in favour of the 1250-unit / 130s figures. The swap's resist gain and resist shred stated in whys[6], late, wants.foe[1] and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Blow is treated as a general-purpose peel tool that can 'knock you out of any commit' at unspecified range. Riot's text puts it at 240 range with a 20/18/16/14/12/10s cooldown, and it deals magic damage. Acceleration Gate's effect on Shock Blast is stated only as 'through his gate' without saying what the gate does.
audit.why: 240 range is the number that changes the fight. Lacerate's radius is 325, so any time Jayce is close enough to knock you back, he is already standing inside your spin — the knockback threat and your best answer occupy the same space. And the gate is not cosmetic: firing Shock Blast through it increases the missile's speed, range and damage, so a gate on the ground is the tell that the next orb is the dangerous one.
audit.corrected: 240 range stated in whys[2], early, mid and breakdown.cooldowns. The gate's speed/range/damage boost stated in whys[0], early, spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'his stance cooldowns are short', which is the opposite of what the data says for the abilities that matter.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16 seconds at rank 1 and Thundering Blow is 20. The genuinely short cooldown is the weapon swap at 6 seconds, and that is the one the page never mentions. Telling a player his cooldowns are short discourages the exact patient trading this lane requires.
audit.corrected: mid and whys[3] rewritten around Shock Blast's real timer, with the 6-second swap identified as the thing that is actually always available.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait the hammer E first' appears with no cooldown, so there is nothing to bait against.
audit.why: Thundering Blow at 20 seconds rank 1 is the longest non-ultimate cooldown in the matchup — longer than Shock Blast — which makes it the correct thing to force out before committing a 130-second ultimate.
audit.corrected: 20s stated in mid and breakdown.cooldowns, and the all-in keyed to a spent Thundering Blow.

audit.why: Jayce gains Move Speed every time he swaps weapons, on a 6-second cooldown. That is why chasing a Jayce who just swapped rarely works, and it is a free tell that he is repositioning rather than committing.
audit.corrected: Folded into the two-item why and the late-game section as the reason the swap governs the fight.

edits.before: Jayce owns the opening — Shock Blast fired through his Acceleration Gate out-ranges everything you have, and at Lvl 1 you only have Cunning Sweep with no Sundering Slam to answer it. Don't walk up to throw a Q he just steps back from; farm at max cone range and accept the chip. Your one tool is Repudiation: brace it into a telegraphed cannon Shock Blast so the blocked champion damage amplifies your next slam instead of eating poke for free. Don't force a trade you can't finish — your cooldowns are too long here and a hammer-stance Thundering Blow knocks you out of any commit.
edits.after: Jayce owns the opening — Shock Blast fired through his Acceleration Gate gains missile speed, range and damage, and at Lvl 1 you only have Cunning Sweep with no Sundering Slam to answer it. Don't walk up to throw a Q he just steps back from; farm at max cone range and accept the chip. Your one tool is Repudiation: brace it into a telegraphed cannon Shock Blast so the blocked champion damage amplifies your next slam instead of eating poke for free. And note Thundering Blow is only 240 range — if he is close enough to knock you back, he is already inside Lacerate.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — his stance cooldowns are short and yours are at their longest, so he pokes and you farm toward 6. Then it flips hard: Public Execution blinks you behind him and suppresses through his Thundering Blow knockback, and the R-passive armor pen plus a Cunning-Sweep-into-Sundering-Slam empowered-auto chain turns a poked-out Jayce into a kill. Bait the hammer E first — if he burns Thundering Blow on your approach, your R re-position has nothing to cancel it. Land the Q cone, dash off Drakehound's Step into the empowered auto, and his squishy frame folds once you're on top of him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — Shock Blast is back every 12 seconds while your cooldowns sit at their longest, so he pokes and you farm toward 6. Then it flips hard: Public Execution blinks 1250 units, suppresses straight through the Thundering Blow knockback and slams him down stunned, and a Cunning-Sweep-into-Sundering-Slam empowered-auto chain turns a poked-out Jayce into a kill. Bait the hammer E first — 240 range and 20 seconds at rank 1, so once he spends it your dash chain has nothing to cancel it. Land the Q cone, dash off Drakehound's Step into the empowered auto.

edits.before: It evens back out — you're a clean AD bruiser with strong ratios, your R-heal sustain and CDR, but Jayce never stops poking and his cannon-to-hammer burst stays relevant from range. You win every time you land Public Execution and close the gap; you lose every time he Acceleration-Gate-kites you with Shock Blast and Thundering Blow before you commit. Don't facecheck or walk into cannon range looking for a fight he won't take — make him over-step into your Q-cone and Repudiation-amplified slam, then R the instant his hammer E is down.
edits.after: It evens back out — you're a clean AD bruiser with strong ratios and short cooldowns, but Jayce never stops poking and his cannon-to-hammer burst stays relevant from range. The swap is only 6 seconds, and it hands him bonus Armor and Magic Resist the moment he picks up the hammer to fight your physical burst. You win every time you land Public Execution and close; you lose every time he gate-kites Shock Blast into Thundering Blow. Make him over-step into your Q cone and a Repudiation-amplified slam.

notes: Every one of the seven level-chart stages contradicted its own why-text on this page — the worst chart-versus-prose disagreement in my slice. Unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'R-passive armor pen', 'R-heal' and 'heal on ability damage', which appear in Riot's text for none of her five abilities and recur across her whole matchup set. One caution on a number I did use: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json gives a single cooldown per slot (Shock Blast 16/14/12/10/8/6, Thundering Blow 20/18/16/14/12/10), but Jayce's two stances have historically tracked their cooldowns separately in game. I wrote the kit's figures because the kit is the stated authority, but if the two stances do run independent timers then 'Shock Blast is back every 12 seconds' understates how often he can throw something, and it is worth confirming before this ships.
